messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Rmd code programmatically from R
parts:
summary.R is not supposed to contain a single line; it must be
annotated by # @knitr, e.g.

# @knitr test
summary(mtcars)

Then inside the Rmd file, you can have

```{r test}
```

There are example scripts in http://yihui.name/knitr/demo/externalization/

And note read_chunk() only reads code chunks; it does not run code.

Regards,
Yihui

> summary(data). Then I run the following in RStudio, but it is not running
> the 'test' chunk. (I did read the documentation in knitr.pdf and consulted
> yihui's site, but there doesn't seem to be any Rmd dedicated documentation)
>
> Best and thanks,
>
> ge

> # My report
>
> ```{r}
> library('knitr')
> data(mtcars)
> ```
>
> ```{r test}
> summary(mtcars)
> ```
>
> ```{r readit}
> read_chunk('summary.R')
> ```
>
> ```{r prepare}
> data = mtcars
> ```
>
> ```{r readit2, ref.label='readit', eval=TRUE}
> # execute
> ```

messages.author: 681871e2b78133be
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Rmd code programmatically from R
parts:
Hi Yihui,

I am sorry, but I cannot parse the Sweave documentation and translate it
to Rmd. What I did and that kind of produce what I want is the following:

Rmd main file:

summary(mtcars)
```

```{r readit, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
data = mtcars[,-1]
out = knit_child('summary.Rmd')
# read_chunk('summary.Rmd')
run_chunk('summary')
```
and

summary.Rmd file:

```{r summary, echo=FALSE}
summary(data)
```
I would expect read_chunk to load the chunk and run to run it, but
instead, I have to knit the chunk to have access to it.
Also, I have been trying to use the string in "out" to include in output
html, but that doesn't do the trick as it is rendered as a R output
string instead of -- I guess -- md format that is later translated to html.

Ideally, I would like to call an R function from another file, like
my_summary(data), this function would include Rmd code that would then
be rendered as html. For example:

my_summary <- function(data){
this is the number of rows: `r nrow(data)`
and this is a summary:
```{r}
summary(data)
```
}

then, from the main file:

```{r}
for (data in my_list){
my_summary(data)
}
```

would produce:
this is the number of rows: 5
and this is a summary:
blabla
this is the number of rows: 15
and this is a summary:
blabla'

and so on. Any suggestion?

Best,

ge
